title: Indian Ocean Islands

cards.b: The Indian Ocean carries most of the world's oil trade. Islands such as the Maldives, Mauritius, Seychelles, Sri Lanka, Madagascar and the Comoros sit on its sea lanes. India's aim of being the 'first responder' and net security provider depends on them, and China is competing for the same ports.
SAGAR was announced in Mauritius in March 2015; MAHASAGAR was announced during Modi's visit there in March 2025 (verify details).

The Maldives lies on key sea lanes. India helped in Operation Cactus (1988) against a coup. Politics swing: 'India Out' campaign and the election of President Mohamed Muizzu (November 2023), who asked Indian military personnel to leave and tilted to China, then repaired ties with Indian aid, a currency swap and credit lines. Modi was guest at Maldivian Independence Day in July 2025. Note the pattern: elections change tone.

Mauritius has a large Indian-origin population (about 70 per cent). India built an airstrip and jetty on Agalega island (inaugurated 2024). The CECPA (2021) was India's first trade pact with an African country. On Chagos, India backs Mauritius's sovereignty claim; a UK-Mauritius treaty (May 2025) transfers sovereignty while the US-UK base on Diego Garcia stays under a long lease.

• Seychelles: Assumption Island military facility plan stalled (2018); coast guard ships and radar help.
  • Sri Lanka: 2022 crisis aid of about 4 billion US dollars; China's Hambantota port on a 99-year lease (2017).
  • Madagascar and Comoros: listening posts, medical aid, and training.
  • Joint: the Colombo Security Conclave (India, Sri Lanka, Maldives, Mauritius; others joined later).

Indian tools: the Navy's presence (Mission-based deployments), the Information Fusion Centre-IOR (Gurugram, 2018), coastal radar chains, HADR (relief after the 2004 tsunami, Operation Sagar Bandhu), lines of credit, Vaccine Maitri (2021), and support for the Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA, 1997). India's Navy is the 'first responder' brand.

China has a base at Djibouti (2017), ports at Gwadar, Hambantota, Kyaukphyu, and research vessels visiting Sri Lanka and the Maldives. The 'string of pearls' theory sees a chain of Chinese-linked ports around India, though critics call it overstated, as many are commercial. Small states practise hedging: they play India, China and the US against each other for aid.

The islands give surveillance, basing, and chokepoint access. Theory link: Mahan's sea power, Alfred Thayer; K.M. Panikkar's India and the Indian Ocean (1945) argued India's security depends on the ocean. Indian Ocean as 'Indian lake' is a Panikkar-era dream: the Navy now builds a blue-water capacity (INS Vikrant, 2022).

Priorities: predictable economic assistance, avoid being seen as big brother, respect domestic politics, maintain HADR roles, deepen the Quad and French/Australian partnerships (Réunion, La Reunion), and help build capacity. UPSC angle: link to Neighbourhood First, SAGAR and the Indo-Pacific.

In May 2019 the UN General Assembly backed a resolution asking the UK to end its administration of the Chagos Archipelago, and India voted in favour.

Structure: geography, frameworks, country cases, tools, China, constraints, way forward.

The ICJ's advisory opinion of February 2019 held that the UK's separation of Chagos from Mauritius was unlawful and that the UK must end its administration as soon as possible.
